title: Understanding the Logistic Regression Equation
text: In logistic regression, the probability of an event is modeled using the logistic function, which is expressed as \( \sigma(\beta_0 + \beta_1x_1 + \beta_2x_2 + \ldots) \). Here, \( \sigma \) is the sigmoid function, and \( \beta \) values are the coefficients from your model.

title: Identifying the Variables
text: For the given problem, identify the values for each variable: \( \beta_0 \) is the intercept, \( \beta_1 \) corresponds to age, and \( \beta_2 \) corresponds to sex. What are the values for a 20-year-old female passenger?

title: Substituting Values into the Equation
text: Substitute the values into the logistic regression equation: \( \beta_0 + \beta_1 \times \text{age} + \beta_2 \times \text{sex} \). Remember, for a female passenger, the sex variable is typically coded as $$1$$.

title: Calculate the Linear Combination
text: Calculate the linear combination of the coefficients and variables: $$\(-1.2$$ + $$(-0.005$$ \times 20) + $$(2.5$$ \times 1)\). What is the result?

title: Applying the Sigmoid Function
text: Once you have the linear combination, apply the sigmoid function \( \sigma(x) $$=$$ \frac{1}{1+e**{-x}} \) to find the probability. What does \( $$\sigma(1.2)$$ \) represent in this context?
